page: Microsoft Azure B16pls_v2 is a burstable, ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Bpsv2 family, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 16 vCPUs backed by 16 physical cores of an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, configured with one thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptographic operations. It is paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring network-attached storage for persistent workloads, and it includes zero dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results reflect the compute density of a 16-core ARM architecture paired with burstable CPU limits. Multi-core compute performance sits in the middle tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 9532.0 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 28890.73. Single-core throughput is constrained, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 1102.0 and lower performance in decompression and text processing. Memory bandwidth reaches 133.81 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 67.63 GB/sec for writes. The instance handles operational workloads steadily, showing 22.0 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and static web serving throughput of 18.67 GB/sec.

The B16pls_v2 offers high core density at a low entry cost for burstable environments, trading consistent peak compute for cost efficiency during periods of low activity. Due to the 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, absence of local disk, and burstable resource allocation, it is best suited for scale-out web serving, continuous integration build agents, microservices, and non-memory-heavy batch processing where baseline compute capacity is punctuated by intermittent processing demands.
description: Microsoft Azure B16pls_v2 is a burstable virtual machine from the Bpsv2 series, powered by a 16-core Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. The instance features 16 physical cores without hyperthreading, 32.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), and hardware AES acceleration. There is no bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on external network volumes for persistent data. Multi-core performance is solid across standard suites, marked by a Geekbench multi-core score of 9532.0, stress-ng multi-core score of 28890.73, and static web throughput of 18.67 GB/sec, while single-core performance remains modest. Given its burstable CPU allocation and low-memory configuration, the instance delivers cost-effective compute capacity for variable workloads such as microservices, web tier deployments, batch workers, and continuous integration pipelines that do not require continuous sustained compute or large memory footprints.
